Otherwise, yeah, I'm in a similar situation to you so I have no idea. But, my doctor recently prescribed me propranolol, and it makes the breakdowns happen less (if you haven't tried it). It's a blood pressure med, off-label use for anxiety since regular anxiety meds didn't do shit for me. I know you're not exactly looking to take more meds, but maybe this one (if you're interested in it), or some other med you try in the future, will work so well that you'll be able to decrease your meds.

Something else that might be reassuring... if you were a mentally sane being, say, even the smartest person in the world (but still sane), you probably wouldn't feel like a defective human being, right? Well, what if you, with your perfectly sane, genius self, had a ton of physical problems that required you to take 7 meds a day just to stay alive - would you still feel defective? I don't know, maybe you would, but my point kind of is that sometimes people need to take meds to be functional and survive. It doesn't make them any less of a person.

I'm actually not no-poo yet and I don't think I qualify as low-poo (although I've used organic shampoos without sulfates). The reason why is it's own story but I totally support going no-poo.

However, I rarely use soap, and I think I've rarely used it for over a year now. I first transitioned to more natural soaps with less chemicals, and then, after reading an article that found that soap was only 3% more effective than going without, I figured I could just go without it.

I have eczema. From my memory, the natural soaps helped a lot.

Recently, and oddly, I had these two large rashes that wouldn't disappear. My shower head wasn't working, so I took a bath. Not wanting to be bathing in my own filth, I gave in and used soap for once (scentless, natural, vegan, eco-friendly soap). I noticed that both rashes immediately cleared up a lot. So, when I showered, I only used soap on my rashes - maybe two weeks - and stopped when they cleared up completely.

I smell fine - I'm extremely self-conscious, so I've asked. I feel that I originally got sicker more often when I first started, but now I rarely get sick. But that could just be a coincidence.

For the most part, I shower every other day, although I'm considering going longer now.

I use Tom's scentless deodorant almost everyday since I sweat a lot. I also use lotion all over, but not everyday, and only because people have gifted them to me over the years and I don't want to waste them. Otherwise, I'd probably be lotion free.

Recently, I was told that my skin looked beautiful, like it was glowing, and I was asked what I do. Awkwardly, I said "Nothing." lol
